svg.title: Identify the extra difference between comparison groups
svg.desc: An explicitly fictional qualitative comparison gives Group A agent X, a warmer culture temperature and a higher proportion positive for marker M; Group B has no agent X, cooler temperature and a lower marker proportion. The values are qualitative and do not duplicate or alter the separate required four-count dataset. Because exposure and temperature vary together, the comparison cannot isolate the effect of one factor. Matching temperature or crossing both factors can help distinguish alternatives. The biological system, developmental time and indirect endpoint limit inference; no individual human risk estimate is provided.

text.tspan: Identify the extra difference between comparison groups
A fictional unmatched comparison changes more than the proposed exposure.
Which difference explains the marker contrast?
Exposure and temperature vary together, so this table does not isolate one cause.
Match the temperature when comparing exposure, or cross both factors in a design.
Keep the biological model, timing and measured endpoint explicit.
A marker difference in this model is not an individual human risk estimate.
